newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end strong on month-end buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end strong on month-end buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed sharply higher on Thursday on month-end buying and in tandem with Wall Street, analysts and traders said.
"There was selective month-end buying, foreign investors stepped in and stocks leaving the overbought zone led the way," said Hector Jimenez, a technical analyst at the Inverlat brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 41.30 points, or 1.14 percent, at 3,672.92. One-third of total volume, million shares traded, was accounted for by cross trades.
"Today's gains were important because they underscored the short-term upward channel in which the bourse is trading. We were close to support at the close yestreday," Jimenez added.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile closed up 1.23 percent at 6,823.86 points.
Some traders said gains on Mexican ADRs listed in New York also bolstered Mexican share prices.
"The market was firm. We thought profit-taking might continue, but funds closing for the month and buoyant (Mexican) ADRs kept hauling the bourse up," a dealer from the Abaco brokerage said.
Market heavyweight Telmex's ADRs ended up 7/8 at 37-7/8, while its L shares advanced 38 centavos to 14.90 pesos.
Dealers noted strong gains by transportation company TMM, whose ADRs gained 7/8 to 6-3/4, while its A shares headed the gainers' list after closing up 5.70 pesos at 42.00 pesos.

"Dealers were buying (TMM) all day, obviously because of the payment they will make for the railroad concession they won. The stock was hit hard long after they tendered their bid and it might even rally further," a trader said.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile closed up 1.23 percent at 6,823.86 points.
TMM announced this week it will pay $280 million as part of its stake in the recently awarded concession to run Mexico's Northeast Railway.
On the broad market, 114 stocks were traded, of which gainers outnumbered decliners by 68 to 27.
Bancrecer financial group headed the decliners, down 10 centavos to 1.22 pesos. Traders noted financial stocks had been hit by fallout from disappointing earnings posted by Banacci last week.
Another leading decliner was industrial stock Tekchem, down 10 centavos to 2.28 pesos.
"Tekchem is almost 60 centavos below its issue price. I don't think it's a bad stock, but it's had more liquidity than was expected so it has been hit hard," one trader said.
